title: Zero-install first run: a stranger gets to green tests in five minutes
summary: Someone who has never seen the catalog lands on a pattern page, copies one line, and has a compliant, tested component in their own project. This is the experience the alternatives already offer and this product does not.

persona.role: Engineer who followed a link and has five minutes
persona.context: Has a Next.js project open. Will not clone a repository, build a server, or edit an absolute path to try something.
persona.goal: To see the claim proven in their own project before deciding whether to care.

trigger: They land on the approval-gate page from a post or a search result.

advantage.claim: Match the one-line baseline without building a CLI or a service, by publishing into installers people already run.
advantage.why_it_holds: It does not hold yet. The alternatives install with one command today. The route to parity that respects the scope limits is to emit static files other tools consume: a shadcn-compatible registry, a skills folder, a plugin manifest. Once there, the same one line would also deliver tests and a pin, which theirs do not.

preconditions: A new project from `npx create-next-app@latest` with TypeScript, unmodified.
No local clone of the catalog.

steps.action: Open the pattern page and find the install line.
steps.expect: One copyable command near the top of the page.

steps.action: Run the one line in the project.

uses.run: <the single install command shown on the page>

steps.expect: The component, its tests, and COMPLIANCE.md appear in the project. No clone, no build step, no absolute path.

steps.action: Run the verification command the install printed.

uses.run: <the verify command printed by the install>

steps.expect: Every test passes in the unmodified create-next-app project.

steps.action: Check what they are allowed to do with the code.
steps.expect: A license that permits using the copied code in their own product.

success.criterion: One command, no clone, no absolute path.
success.check: s2 is a single command that fetches everything it needs.

success.criterion: Landing to green tests in under five minutes.
success.check: Wall-clock time from opening the page in s1 to a passing run in s3 is under five minutes on a normal connection.

success.criterion: It works in an unmodified create-next-app project.
success.check: s3 passes with no edit to tsconfig.json or package.json beyond what the install itself made.

success.criterion: The license permits what the page tells the reader to do.
success.check: LICENSE.md grants use, modification, and redistribution of the copied code.

gaps.summary: The site is not deployed, so no pattern page can be reached.
gaps.fix: Reconnect or redeploy the Vercel project.

gaps.summary: Nothing can be installed without cloning the repository.
gaps.evidence: The adoption section on each pattern page begins with `git clone`. Both packages are private and unpublished.
gaps.fix: Choose one or more: static shadcn-compatible registry JSON emitted by the site build; a skills/ folder installable with `npx skills add`; the MCP server on npm or in a Claude Code plugin. See docs/research/landscape.md, UX moves 5 to 7.

gaps.summary: Reference files copied straight from patterns/<id>/react fail every test unless the consumer's tsconfig sets jsx to react-jsx. Files returned by scaffold_pattern no longer do: they carry per-file JSX pragmas (mcp-server/DESIGN.md amendment 15, 2026-11-12).
gaps.evidence: Baseline run of ground-a-coding-agent: 13 of 13 tests fail under "jsx": "preserve". The adoption section on each pattern page copies the reference directory, which has no pragmas.
gaps.fix: Have the one-line install deliver the scaffold output rather than the raw reference files, or add the same pragmas to the reference files.

gaps.summary: The license reserves all rights while the product asks people to copy its code.
gaps.fix: Choose a license that permits the adoption the product is built for.

automation.schedule: Run in plan mode now. Once the gaps close, run it after every site deploy: it is the smoke test for the front door.
automation.notes: This journey is the definition of done for launch. Three of its four gaps are owner decisions; run it in plan mode to get the options laid out side by side.
